rows.prompt: Image 1 is the photo to convert and Image 2 is a lighting reference only. Keep Image 1 exactly as it is in framing, camera position, lens and every object: the same single-storey house with its dark tiled hip roof, the cream rendered front wall and white plantation shutters, the charcoal rendered fence with the number 5, the stone pillar and letterbox, the white louvred side gate, the dark timber paling fence on the left, the vertical timber-look orange garage door with the number 5 on the charcoal pier beside it, the satellite dish on the roof, the palms and gardens, the sloping asphalt road with its yellow kerb line and the flagstone edging on the right. Nothing is added, removed, moved or rebuilt, and the framing is not cropped, zoomed or shifted. Relight it to early-evening twilight about twenty minutes after sunset, matching the light and sky of Image 2 but not its composition. All direct sunlight is gone, so there are no sun patches, no hard shadows on the road and no bright highlights on the palm fronds. The sky is a clean, clear gradient from soft mid blue overhead to pale cream at the horizon with almost no cloud. The existing downlights in the eave above the garage door are on and throw warm pools of light down the face of the garage door and onto the driveway, so the orange timber door glows a rich warm orange. The existing entry light by the front door is on, and the front window behind the shutters glows a soft warm amber from inside. The road, fences, gardens and palms stay clearly readable in soft, even, cool dusk light with natural greens, bright rather than moody. High-end twilight real estate photography, photorealistic, sharp.
